findings.description: The new `return` inside the iOS 17 branch exits `tearDown()` before `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()` on lines 36-37. BaseTestCase.tearDown (BaseTestCase.swift:119-122) is therefore also never reached, so the intended skip of the theme reset additionally skips all cleanup. This triggers for testSelectBottomPlacement on any device and for every OnboardingTests test on iPad via `|| iPad()`.
findings.failureMode: On iPad (and for testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone) the app is left running and superclass teardown is skipped, leaking app/profile/theme state into the next test.
findings.title: tearDown early return skips app termination and super.tearDown

findings.description: XCTest only discovers methods prefixed with `test`, and AGENTS.md rule 6 requires that prefix, so `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` is never executed and no caller invokes it (grep finds no call site). AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan:371 still selects `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`, which no longer exists. The fix is to restore the `test` prefix; the flakiness fix in longPressBookmarkAndReachShareOptions then actually applies to this case.
findings.failureMode: The bookmarks Reminders share test silently never runs in any plan, losing coverage while the Accessibility plan references a non-existent test.
findings.title: Renaming test to verify disables XCTest discovery

findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to trigger.expect regardless of posture. The reference FlowRunStateTriggerFields (flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx:24-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:30-31) both switch to trigger.after when posture is Proactive ('Stays in'), and the stories encode the same mapping. With Proactive selected here, the chosen status lands in expect and after stays empty, inverting the intended 'stays in status' semantics.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-pool automation fires on absence of the status event instead of when the pool stays in that status for the within period.
findings.title: Work pool Proactive status stored in expect instead of after

findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to trigger.expect regardless of posture. FlowRunStateTriggerFields (flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx:24-25) and DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:30-31) both use trigger.after for Proactive ('Stays in') and trigger.expect for Reactive. This component never writes trigger.after, so a Proactive selection is submitted as an expected event rather than a stay-in state.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-queue automation triggers on the status event not occurring, the opposite of the 'Stays in' behavior the user selected.
findings.title: Work queue Proactive status stored in expect instead of after

findings.description: ''.split('\n') returns [''] in JavaScript (verified with node), so lines.length > 0 is always true and the undefined branch is dead; clearing the textarea stores [''] and a trailing newline appends ''. The Zod schema accepts any string in expect, and the backend expects() only treats an empty expect set as match-any, so [''] matches no real event instead of meaning no expected events. Empty lines must be filtered before calling field.onChange.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom-events textarea submits expect=[''], creating a reactive automation that can never match any event.
findings.title: Custom trigger stores empty string as an expected event

findings.description: The diff flips compilerOptions.strict from true to false in tsconfig.app.json, weakening the type-checking enforcement that validate:types (tsc -b --noEmit) relies on and violating repository mandate 11 requiring strict mode. Nothing in the new components requires relaxed checking; they already guard optional values. Restore strict: true.
findings.failureMode: Null/undefined and implicit-any errors across the whole ui-v2 app pass type validation and surface as runtime crashes instead of compile-time failures.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled

findings.description: This is the only bare parseInt( in ui-v2/src; biome.json sets style/useNumberNamespace to error and CI runs biome ci (.github/workflows/ui-v2-checks.yml), so the check fails on this line. It also diverges from every sibling threshold field using Number(...): clearing the input gives parseInt('') === NaN (verified with node) instead of 0, and decimals are silently truncated. Use Number(e.target.value) like the other trigger fields.
findings.failureMode: The biome ci job fails on this file, and clearing the work-pool threshold stores NaN instead of following the sibling validation path.
findings.title: Bare parseInt violates Biome useNumberNamespace and yields NaN

findings.description: After Action.SelectLightTheme, which taps lightThemeView in registerSettingsNavigation.swift, line 53 reads darkThemeView and asserts it is "1". The base read lightThemeView, and testCheckDisplaySettingsDefault shows only the selected theme has value "1", so the dark view is "0" after selecting light. Fix line 53 to read AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.lightThemeView.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails on every run at the light-theme assertion and never verifies light selection.
findings.title: Light-theme assertion reads darkThemeView

findings.description: The test is on TopSitesSettingsViewController (Shortcuts page) after tapping the Shortcuts cell directly, and that controller and its SettingsTableViewController base add no Done right-bar button; Done exists on HomePageSettingViewController/AppSettings root. The base order navigator.goto(NewTabScreen) then Done unwound one level first, matching the unchanged validateNumberOfTopSitesDisplayed pattern, while Done-then-goto patterns elsewhere use nowAt. findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection times out in waitAndTap on the non-existent Done button on the Shortcuts page and fails before checking Top Sites removal.
findings.title: Done tapped before navigator unwind from Shortcuts page

findings.description: The diff deletes the call checkCopiedUrl() (base line 71) from testClipboard, leaving its only remaining mention commented out in testClipboardPasteAndGo. checkCopiedUrl was the assertion that UIPasteboard.general.string equals the URL bar value on iOS < 16, and the later paste assertion in testClipboard is guarded by #available(iOS 17, *). No replacement verification is added, so restore the call.
findings.failureMode: On iOS < 16 a wrong or empty clipboard copy passes testClipboard silently because no clipboard assertion runs on that path.
findings.title: testClipboard no longer verifies copied URL

findings.description: The rename replaced pageActionStack with a second browserActionStack in the stacks list, so trailingPageActionStack arranged subviews are never included. updateActionStack sets alpha=0 on newly added buttons (line 371) and only updateToolbarLayout restores alpha=1.0 for views in this list, as the base did via pageActionStack. Fix: use trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews as the fourth term.
findings.failureMode: Newly added trailing page-action buttons remain at alpha 0 and are invisible in the address toolbar.
findings.title: Trailing page actions omitted from fade-in, stay invisible

findings.description: toolbar.leadingAnchor now equals rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor while toolbar.trailingAnchor equals rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor (line 449); the base used leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor for leading. Since the right skeleton bar's leading is pinned to the container's trailingAnchor (line 474), the toolbar's leading ends up beyond its trailing. Fix: restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.failureMode: With swiping-tabs enabled the toolbar gets unsatisfiable/negative-width constraints and is collapsed or pushed off-screen.
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchor pinned to right instead of left skeleton bar

findings.description: hasPageActions now checks leadingPageActionStack, but the base checked pageActionStack, which this diff renames to trailingPageActionStack. The divider sits between locationView and trailingPageActionStack (constraints at lines 271-275), so its width must follow the trailing stack. Fix: check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: When leading and trailing page-action emptiness differ, the address-bar divider is missing beside trailing actions or shown spuriously with none.
findings.title: Divider width keyed to leading instead of trailing page actions

findings.description: isLandscape is assigned from UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation (deprecated since iOS 13, sole use in the repo per grep) and is never referenced again in setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout, despite the comment claiming layout adjustments. This yields unused-value and deprecation warnings, which configurations with SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=YES turn into build failures. Fix: remove the variable and comment.
findings.failureMode: Builds that treat Swift warnings as errors fail, and the claimed landscape adjustment silently does nothing.
findings.title: Unused isLandscape using deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: LaunchCoordinator previously called onboardingService.handleAction synchronously inside the @MainActor onActionTap closure; the diff wraps it in an unstructured Task at line 273, so handleBottomButtonAction returns before handleAction runs. handleAction has side effects (presenting sync sign-in/instructions popup, opening Settings, endOnboarding) and calls completion to advance or complete the flow, while onDismiss/onComplete in the same file nil onboardingService and finish launch. Because the Task strongly captures the already-unwrapped service, nil-ing self.onboardingService does not cancel it, so any same-turn interleaving (e.g. a tap followed synchronously by skip/dismissal, or a second action) can run the deferred action after dismissal/completion.
findings.failureMode: A deferred onboarding action can present a popup/sign-in, open Settings, or complete/advance the flow after onboarding was already dismissed, instead of being ordered before dismissal like the previous synchronous call.
findings.title: Onboarding action deferred into unstructured Task loses synchronous ordering

findings.description: The diff deletes DownloadToast's nested 'struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }' and replaces both UX.buttonSize uses with the literal 40 at lines 192-193. AGENTS.md mandate 13 requires UI constant values to be defined in a nested UX struct and lists scattered literals as the failure criterion. The value is now duplicated in two places, so a later size change must edit both literals and can update only one.
findings.failureMode: The duplicated 40 literals violate the mandatory UX-struct rule and can diverge on a future edit, making the close button non-square (height != width).
findings.title: DownloadToast close-button size inlined as magic literals instead of UX struct

findings.description: The guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` exempts None, so `return rendered` returns None from a method declared `-> str` when the executor result has no "result" key. I verified this with a fake executor returning {} (render_template returned None) and with basedpyright and mypy, both reporting an incompatible `str | None` return at line 40, which fails the style CI type gates. TemplateTransformNode._run then calls len(rendered) at template_transform_node.py:69 inside a handler that only catches TemplateRenderError, so the node raises TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; the fix is to raise TemplateRenderError for any non-str rendered value, including None.
findings.failureMode: A missing or None "result" from the code executor escapes as None, failing type-check CI and crashing template-transform execution with TypeError on len() instead of a handled node failure.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing result

findings.description: Base used `if !gtk.exists()` and the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 still does, but line 243 uses `if gtk.exists()`. On a fresh tools directory the embedded linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never written, yet bundle_project unconditionally passes `--plugin gtk` to linuxdeploy (lines 201-202). Fix to `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: First AppImage bundle on a clean machine fails in linuxdeploy because the GTK plugin script is missing.
findings.title: GTK plugin condition inverted, fresh installs never write it

findings.description: Base wrote the file first and then called set_permissions; line 312 now calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write on line 313. Every caller except the inverted GTK block is guarded by `!exists()`, so the path does not exist yet and set_permissions fails with ENOENT. Restore write-then-set_permissions order.
findings.failureMode: prepare_tools fails on first use for AppRun, linuxdeploy and plugin files, so AppImage bundling cannot proceed.
findings.title: Permissions set before file is written

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError> at line 309, replacing std::io::Result. prepare_tools returns crate::Result<PathBuf> and uses `?` on this function (lines 232, 239, 259), but crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs has no From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error (only From<io::Error> and From<anyhow::Error>, which are not transitive). This is a `?` conversion (E0277) compile failure on Linux; return io::Result or add a proper conversion.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile for Linux targets.
findings.title: FileWriteError does not convert into crate::Error, breaking compilation

findings.description: Line 235 maps i686 to the linuxdeploy arch name and line 236 uses it for the local file, and base used that same variable in the download URL. Line 238 now interpolates raw `{arch}`, requesting linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage for 32-bit x86 builds instead of the mapped i386-style asset name used elsewhere (lines 25 and 139). Restore `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage builds fail to download linuxdeploy (404) and prepare_tools returns an error.
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL bypasses arch mapping

findings.description: Mandate 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes. FileWriteError at line 286 derives only Debug and manually implements Display (line 291) and std::error::Error (line 300). Replace the manual impls with a thiserror derive (or keep std::io::Error, which crate::Error already converts from).
findings.failureMode: The new error type violates the repository thiserror mandate and is inconsistent with the crate error type in error.rs.
findings.title: Custom error enum does not use thiserror

findings.description: Running `rustfmt --check` on this file reports a single diff wrapping line 312, whose long set_permissions/map_err chain exceeds the project max_width=100 in rustfmt.toml. Mandate 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass. Reformat the chain as rustfmt specifies.
findings.failureMode: The cargo fmt --check CI gate fails on this file.
findings.title: Changed line is not rustfmt-formatted

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops with j <= keys_result->numkeys (base used j < numkeys), so the final iteration reads keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] into a buffer allocated for only numkeys ints at line 1110. getKeysPrepareResult sizes the heap keys array to exactly numkeys, and the inline keysbuf entry past numkeys is a zeroed keyReference with pos 0, so a valid single-key cluster command hashes argv[0] as an extra key while larger key counts read/write out of bounds. Fix the bound to j < keys_result->numkeys (the slot_buffer itself is unnecessary).
findings.failureMode: Valid same-slot cluster commands are spuriously rejected as CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, and with heap-sized key arrays the server corrupts the heap or crashes.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads and writes past key/slot arrays

findings.description: The new slot_buffer uses malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating AGENTS.md rule 2 requiring zmalloc/zfree outside zmalloc.c; server.h marks malloc/free deprecated for this reason. Verified by running make -C src cluster.o REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror", which fails with -Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations errors on all three calls, also violating rule 4. Use zmalloc/zfree or remove the unused buffer entirely.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails to compile cluster.c, and the allocation bypasses Redis memory tracking.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free breaks zmalloc mandate and -Werror build

findings.description: Line 31 binds the status select to trigger.after when posture is Proactive, unlike the work-pool, work-queue, and custom components in this diff which always use trigger.expect. The backend EventTrigger uses expect for the expected events in both postures (Reactive responds to their presence, Proactive to their absence) and after only as the prerequisite event that starts the window; with expect left empty the backend's expects() matches any event. Selecting Proactive + Ready therefore creates after=["prefect.deployment.ready"] with no expected status, and switching posture also orphans the previously selected status in the other field so both can be submitted together. Fix: always bind the status select to trigger.expect.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive deployment-status automation does not expect the selected status event, so it evaluates against any event after the status instead of the absence/presence of that status and fires incorrectly or not at all.
findings.title: Proactive deployment status written to trigger.after instead of trigger.expect

findings.description: The diff changes "strict": true to "strict": false in tsconfig.app.json, which directly violates AGENTS.md rule 11 requiring strict mode enabled with the validate:types script (tsc -b --noEmit) in package.json. This weakens the type-checking enforcement for the whole ui-v2 app rather than fixing any type errors in the new components. Code with implicit any, unchecked null/undefined, or unsound assignments will now pass tsc -b --noEmit and the build. Fix: restore "strict": true and fix any resulting type errors in the new files.
findings.failureMode: validate:types and the production build silently accept type-unsafe code that strict checking would reject, allowing null/undefined defects to reach runtime as crashes.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled

findings.description:
Lines 38-39 split the textarea on "
" and guard only on lines.length > 0, but String.split never returns an empty array: "".split("
") is [""] and "a
".split("
") is ["a", ""] (verified by execution). Clearing the textarea therefore stores expect=[""] instead of undefined, and ending the input with a newline stores a trailing "" alongside the real events. The AutomationWizardSchema accepts any string array, so the empty event name is submitted and matches no real event. Fix: filter out empty (and whitespace-only) lines and pass undefined when none remain.
findings.failureMode: A cleared or trailing-newline custom trigger is submitted expecting an empty-string event that never occurs, so a Reactive automation never fires (and a Proactive one can fire spuriously).
findings.title: Custom trigger textarea stores empty-string expected events

findings.description: Line 78 uses the global parseInt(e.target.value) with no radix, while every sibling component in this diff (and the existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields) uses Number(e.target.value) and the rest of ui-v2 uses Number.parseInt(value, 10). ui-v2/biome.json sets the style rule useNumberNamespace to "error", which forbids the global parseInt, so biome check/lint fails on this line. parseInt also parses differently from Number, e.g. parseInt("1e3") is 1 instead of 1000 and parseInt("") is NaN (verified by execution). Fix: use Number(e.target.value) like the other trigger field components.
findings.failureMode: The biome lint gate errors on the global parseInt, and threshold values such as exponent-form number input are parsed to the wrong number.
findings.title: Global parseInt without radix for work-pool threshold

findings.description: prepare_tools returns crate::Result<PathBuf> (Result<T, crate::Error>) and uses `write_and_make_executable(...)?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259, but the helper now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>. I grepped crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs: crate::Error has #[from] conversions for io::Error and others but no From<FileWriteError>, and a rustc probe of this shape fails with E0277 `the trait From<FileWriteError> is not implemented for Error`. The module is compiled under #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], so Linux builds of tauri-bundler fail. Fix by returning std::io::Result as before or adding a From conversion into crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux, blocking all AppImage bundling.
findings.title: FileWriteError does not convert to crate::Error, breaking Linux compilation

findings.description: The base code called fs::write then fs::set_permissions; the new code calls fs::set_permissions first. Every caller only invokes this helper when the target does not exist yet (e.g. `if !apprun.exists()`, `if !linuxdeploy.exists()`, `if !gstreamer.exists()`), and chmod on a nonexistent path returns NotFound. On a fresh tools directory the first call therefore errors before any bytes are written. Fix by writing the file first and setting mode 0o770 afterwards.
findings.failureMode: On a clean machine prepare_tools fails with a permissions NotFound error and no AppImage tools are installed.
findings.title: Permissions are set before the file is written, so first-time writes always fail

findings.description: The base code used `if !gtk.exists()` and the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 still uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`, but the GTK block was changed to `if gtk.exists()`. On a fresh tools directory linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is therefore never written, while bundle_project always passes `--plugin gtk` to linuxdeploy (lines 201-202). Fix by restoring `if !gtk.exists()` (or writing unconditionally).
findings.failureMode: linuxdeploy fails because the gtk plugin script is missing from the tools directory on first run.
findings.title: Inverted existence check prevents the GTK plugin from ever being installed on fresh setups

findings.description: Line 235 maps arch `i686` to linuxdeploy_arch and line 236 names the local file with that mapped value, and the base code also used linuxdeploy_arch in the download URL. The changed line uses `{arch}` in the URL, so for i686 targets the download requests linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage while the expected/installed artifact is the mapped name. For other arches the values coincide, which confines the breakage to i686. Fix by using `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL as before.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage bundling fails to download linuxdeploy (wrong release asset name / 404).
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL uses raw arch instead of the mapped linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires all custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes and lists manual Display/Error implementations as the failure criterion. The new FileWriteError at lines 285-307 derives only Debug and hand-implements Display and std::error::Error. This is independent of the missing From conversion: adding that conversion alone would still leave the mandate violated. Fix by deriving thiserror::Error with #[error] messages, or by removing the custom type and returning io::Result.
findings.failureMode: The new error type violates the repository's mandatory error-handling convention and is rejected under the AGENTS.md compliance rules.
findings.title: Custom FileWriteError manually implements Display/Error instead of using thiserror

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass with rustfmt.toml (max_width=100). I ran the toolchain rustfmt in --check mode on this file and it reports a diff at line 312, rewrapping the 101-column set_permissions call onto two lines. No other hunk in the file produced a rustfmt diff. Fix by running cargo fmt on the file.
findings.failureMode: The required formatting gate `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this file.
findings.title: Changed line 312 exceeds rustfmt max_width and fails cargo fmt --check

findings.description: The endpoint uses @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") instead of TEAM_ADMIN. RolesGuard.hasMinimumRole with TEAM_ROLES=[TEAM_OWNER,TEAM_ADMIN,TEAM_MEMBER] passes a MEMBER membership (index 2 <= 2), while the parallel organizations invite controller, the TRPC createInvite handler (OWNER/ADMIN fallback), the PR description, and the new e2e test expecting 403 for a MEMBER all require admin. Fix the decorator to @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Any regular team member can mint a shareable invite link/token that lets outsiders join the team, bypassing the admin-only authorization.
findings.title: Non-admin team members can create invite links

findings.description: The new-token branch returns token: newToken.identifier, where identifier is the constant `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` set on line 90, not the random hex token stored on line 91. The base code returned `token`, the existing-token branch on line 79 returns existingToken.token, and buildInviteLink is called with the real token, so data.token is constant across requests and is not contained in inviteLink. Fix by returning newToken.token (or token).
findings.failureMode: API consumers receive a predictable non-secret identifier as token that cannot redeem the invite, and repeat calls return the same token value.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of the secret token

findings.description: The diff changes `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink` to `if (isOrgContext)`, swapping destinations verified against the base file via git show. Regular teams (isOrgContext=false) now get the /signup?token=...&callbackUrl=gettingStarted orgInviteLink, while organizations/org sub-teams now get /teams?token=..., contrary to the variable names and the PR description. Fix by restoring `if (!isOrgContext)`.
findings.failureMode: Every invite link from createInvite (including existing TRPC and org API callers) routes invitees to the wrong flow for its team/org context.
findings.title: buildInviteLink org/team condition inverted

findings.description: The deleted line converted the keyword with unicode_escape (and doubled \u) so it could match WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs, which are stored as json.dumps(...) text with ensure_ascii defaulting to true (core/repositories/sqlalchemy_workflow_execution_repository.py:152). The new code searches for the raw keyword, so a Chinese keyword such as a non-ASCII term no longer matches the stored \uXXXX representation in the JSON text columns. Fix by retaining the unicode-escaped form (then LIKE-escaping it) for the inputs/outputs conditions.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow app logs with a non-ASCII keyword returns no results even when matching runs exist.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search loses unicode-escaped JSON matching

findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes %, _ and backslash with a backslash prefix and its docstring requires ESCAPE '\', but this query declares ESCAPE '|'. With '|' as the escape character the backslash in patterns such as %50\%% is a literal and % remains a wildcard, which I verified changes LIKE matching for escaped patterns. Use ESCAPE '\' (or escape with '|' instead) so the pattern and clause agree.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback text search returns wrong or no documents for queries containing %, _ or backslash, and wildcard injection remains possible.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE escape character does not match helper escaping

findings.description: The Python literal '\\\\' renders SQL text ESCAPE '\\' containing two backslash characters. Clickzetta connections in this same file set cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote' (line 148), under which backslashes in string literals are literal, so the ESCAPE value is two characters rather than the single backslash that escape_like_pattern produces and SQL requires. Render a single-character ESCAPE '\' in the SQL text.
findings.failureMode: Clickzetta fallback LIKE search fails with an invalid ESCAPE error or does not treat \% and \_ as literals.
findings.title: Clickzetta ESCAPE clause is a two-character string

findings.description: The contains, start-with and end-with branches all pass escape='\\' together with escape_like_pattern, but the not-contains branch calls notlike without an escape argument, so SQLAlchemy renders no ESCAPE clause. The escaped pattern then relies on an implicit backend-default escape character; on backends without a backslash default (verified with SQLite) a search value such as 50% is not treated literally. Add escape='\\' to the notlike call to match its sibling branches.
findings.failureMode: A 'not contains' metadata filter containing %, _ or backslash can fail to exclude matching documents or exclude the wrong ones.
findings.title: 'not contains' metadata filter omits the ESCAPE clause

findings.description: The new local variable escapedPattern is camelCase, violating mandatory repository rule 16 requiring snake_case for Python variables and functions; every other variable added in this diff uses snake_case. Rename it to escaped_pattern.
findings.failureMode: The change fails the repository's mandatory Python naming compliance rule for the new production helper.
findings.title: New helper variable uses camelCase instead of snake_case

findings.description: The rename of pageActionStack to trailingPageActionStack was applied here as a second browserActionStack (already listed on line 329), so trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews are never included in stacks. updateActionStack sets newly added buttons to alpha 0 (line 371) and updateToolbarLayout is the code that resets alpha to 1.0, so newly added trailing page-action buttons remain invisible. Fix by using trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews on this line.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page-action buttons in the address toolbar stay at alpha 0 and are invisible to the user.
findings.title: Trailing page actions omitted from alpha reset

findings.description: The leading constraint was changed from leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, while the next line pins toolbar.trailingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor. The right skeleton bar is positioned off-screen to the right (leading equals the container trailing anchor), so the toolbar leading anchor is placed beyond its trailing anchor, creating unsatisfiable/negative-width constraints when swiping tabs is enabled. Fix by restoring leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor for the leading constraint.
findings.failureMode: With swiping tabs enabled, Auto Layout cannot satisfy the toolbar constraints and the address toolbar is mispositioned or collapses.
findings.title: Toolbar leading pinned to right skeleton bar

findings.description: This line changed the former pageActionStack (renamed to trailingPageActionStack) check to leadingPageActionStack. The divider sits immediately before trailingPageActionStack (its trailing anchor is pinned to trailingPageActionStack.leadingAnchor), so its width must depend on trailing actions. When leading and trailing action counts differ, the divider is shown or hidden incorrectly. Fix by checking trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: The address-bar divider appears when there are no trailing page actions or disappears when trailing actions are present.
findings.title: Divider visibility checks leading instead of trailing stack

findings.description: The new isLandscape constant is never read anywhere in setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout or elsewhere in the file (grep shows only this declaration). Swift emits an unused-immutable warning for it and the claimed landscape layout adjustment never happens. Fix by removing the declaration and its comment, or by actually using the value.
findings.failureMode: The build gains an unused-variable warning and dead code that performs no landscape adjustment.
findings.title: Unused isLandscape variable added

findings.description: The diff deletes DownloadToast's nested `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and this changed line replaces `UX.buttonSize` with the literal 40 for the close button height. AGENTS.md rule 13 requires UI constants and magic numbers to be defined in a nested UX struct, and no replacement constant was added in DownloadToast or Toast.UX (verified by reading Toast.swift).

findings.description: Base code built keyword_like_val via keyword.encode('unicode_escape') with \u doubled for LIKE, matching WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs stored by json.dumps (ensure_ascii=True, e.g. in sqlalchemy_workflow_execution_repository.py) as literal \uXXXX text. The new code at line 93 only applies escape_like_pattern to the raw trimmed keyword, so a non-ASCII keyword stays literal characters. Verified with json.dumps({'k':'中文'}): the stored text contains \u4e2d\u6587, not the literal characters, so the new ILIKE pattern cannot match it.

findings.description: escape_like_pattern produces \%, \_ and \\ sequences documented for use with ESCAPE '\', but line 298 declares ESCAPE '|'. With '|' as the escape character the backslash is a literal and %/_ remain wildcards, and any '|' in the query becomes an escape introducer. Demonstrated in SQLite LIKE semantics: pattern %50\%% with ESCAPE '|' matched '50\XYZ off' instead of '50% off', while ESCAPE '\' matched correctly.
findings.failureMode: IRIS full-text fallback searches containing %, _ or backslash return wildcard matches and miss the literal text, so the intended LIKE-injection fix does not work on this backend.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback uses ESCAPE '|' while escape_like_pattern escapes with backslash

findings.description: The contains (line 1203), start-with (1211) and end-with (1215) branches pass escape="\\" to like(), but the new not-contains branch at line 1207 calls json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%") with no escape argument. Without an explicit ESCAPE clause the \%, \_ and \\ sequences from escape_like_pattern are not guaranteed to be treated as escapes (for example SQLite LIKE has no default escape, where NOT LIKE '%50\%%' without ESCAPE fails to exclude '50% off'). The fix is to pass escape="\\" to notlike() as in the sibling branches.

findings.title: Metadata 'not contains' filter escapes value but omits escape argument

findings.description: The new validator only checks that name is a non-empty string, then returns 'data as CreateScheduleInput' without validating schedule or eventTypeId. It replaces the ZCreateInputSchema contract (zod array of {start: Date, end: Date} and numeric eventTypeId), so input like {name:'Work', schedule:'bad', eventTypeId:'abc'} is returned as valid typed input and malformed data reaches the create-schedule POST instead of a validation error. It also throws generic Error objects rather than following the separated Zod schema pattern.
findings.failureMode: Callers trusting the validator send malformed schedule payloads that fail server-side instead of being rejected at validation.
findings.title: validateCreateScheduleInput casts unchecked fields to CreateScheduleInput

findings.description: Lines 39-46 use single-quoted strings while biome.json sets javascript.formatter.quoteStyle to 'double'. Running biome 2.3.10 format on this file exits 1 and reports the formatter would rewrite these lines. Reformat the file with Biome.

findings.description: In template_renderer.py render_template does result.get("result") and only rejects non-strings when rendered is not None, so a missing key or {"result": None} from an injected CodeExecutor returns None despite the -> str contract. TemplateTransformNode._run then calls len(rendered) at template_transform_node.py:69 inside a try that only catches TemplateRenderError, so it raises TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; I reproduced this with a stub executor returning {} and {"result": None}, both returning None then failing len() while an int result correctly raises TemplateRenderError. Fix the guard to reject any non-string including None (if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)).
findings.failureMode: A code executor response without a string result makes TemplateTransformNode._run raise TypeError on len(None) instead of returning a clean FAILED result.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing result, crashing node on len()

findings.description: The changed hashTypeSet call removes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL that the base had and that hincrbyCommand still uses at t_hash.c:2506. In hashTypeSet, without that flag LISTPACK_EX expiry is cleared (t_hash.c:961-963) and HT expiry is persisted/removed (t_hash.c:989-991), so HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1 loses the TTL on the master itself. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with an expiration clears that expiration on the master, leaving the field persistent and diverging from the intended KEEPTTL semantics.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT drops field TTL on master

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but seven robj arguments are supplied: hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, and newobj. Its implementation in networking.c:4158-4172 allocates and copies only argc varargs, so newobj (the final float value) is dropped and the propagated command is HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field. hsetexParseArgs rejects that shape with an arity error (fields position i >= argc-3), so replicas/AOF never apply the increment; argc must be 7.
findings.failureMode: Every replicated or AOF-replayed HINCRBYFLOAT becomes a malformed HSETEX without a value and is rejected, causing replica/AOF divergence from the master.
findings.title: Replicated HSETEX omits the incremented value

findings.description: addHashFieldToReply was static in the base and a repo-wide search shows all callers are in src/t_hash.c (lines 2605, 2621, 2685, 2810) with no declaration in server.h. Removing static exports this internal helper to other compilation units, violating AGENTS.md rule 7 that functions only used within a single source file must be declared static. Restore the static keyword.
findings.failureMode: The internal helper becomes an externally visible symbol, polluting the global namespace and failing the repository static-helper compliance rule.
findings.title: File-local helper loses static linkage

AGENTS.md rule 2 requires file-scoped namespaces, and .editorconfig sets csharp_style_namespace_declarations=file_scoped with IDE0161 as warning for this path (the silent override only covers Shared/runtime). findings.description: The new controller guards createInvite with @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") at line 32. RolesGuard treats this as a minimum role over TEAM_ROLES [OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER] (hasMinimumRole in roles.guard.ts), so a plain MEMBER passes, while the parallel OrganizationsTeamsInviteController and the tRPC createInvite handler require ADMIN/OWNER (TEAM_ADMIN / fallbackRoles [OWNER, ADMIN]). Fix by changing the decorator to @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN") so the e2e case expecting 403 for a MEMBER holds.
findings.failureMode: Any non-admin team member can mint a shareable invite link and let arbitrary people join the team, an authorization bypass.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows any team member, not only admins

findings.description: Base code returned the random hex `token`; the diff returns `newToken.identifier`, which is the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` set a few lines above, while inviteLink is built from the real `token`. A caller therefore receives a predictable, team-constant value that is not the persisted verification token and is not contained in inviteLink, contradicting the existing-token branch which returns existingToken.token. Fix by returning `token` (or newToken.token).
findings.failureMode: Every invite response carries a wrong, identical token for the team, so sharing the returned token fails and repeated requests do not yield a new token.
findings.title: createInvite returns the token identifier instead of the generated token

findings.description: Base code returned the `/teams?token=` link when `!isOrgContext` and fell through to the `/signup?...callbackUrl=` org link otherwise; the diff flips this to `if (isOrgContext)` returning the teams link. Regular teams now get the org signup link and organization (sub-)teams get the plain teams link, opposite to the variable naming (orgInviteLink) and prior behavior relied on by existing tRPC callers. Fix by restoring `if (!isOrgContext)`.
findings.failureMode: Invite links route to the wrong flow for both regular teams and organization teams on every createInvite call.
findings.title: buildInviteLink org/context condition is inverted

findings.description: The BUILD002 error condition now also requires '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1', whereas the base required only a servicing build with unused baseline package references. docs/BuildErrors.md states BUILD002 appears in servicing builds, which should not change references between assemblies or packages, with no first-patch exception, and nothing in the new code re-establishes the check for later patches. In a 10.0.2 servicing build (AspNetCorePatchVersion=2), removing a BaselinePackageReference from a shipping package leaves UnusedBaselinePackageReference non-empty but no longer produces BUILD002.
findings.failureMode: A breaking package-reference removal in a 10.0.2 or later servicing update builds silently instead of failing with BUILD002.
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing reference check disabled after first patch

findings.description: The diff replaces the file-scoped declaration 'namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;' with a block-scoped namespace at line 16 plus opening and closing braces. AGENTS.md rule 2 mandates file-scoped namespace declarations in all C# files and .editorconfig sets csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped with IDE0161 at warning severity. Restoring the semicolon-terminated file-scoped namespace and removing the added braces fixes the violation.
findings.failureMode: The changed file violates the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule and reports IDE0161 for this file.
findings.title: Test file reverts to block-scoped namespace

findings.description: The loop at src/cluster.c:1112 uses j <= keys_result->numkeys, so it executes for j==numkeys. At that iteration keys_result->keys[j] is past the valid key references and slot_buffer[j] at line 1115 writes past the numkeys-element buffer allocated at line 1110. For a single-key cluster command it hashes argv[keys[1].pos] from uninitialized/out-of-bounds data, producing a spurious CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT or heap corruption instead of the key's slot.
findings.failureMode: Any cluster command with keys can crash, corrupt the heap, or be wrongly rejected as cross-slot.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads and writes past key/slot arrays

findings.description: Line 1110 uses malloc() and lines 1120 and 1124 use free() for slot_buffer, contrary to the repository mandate to use zmalloc/zfree outside zmalloc.c. Compiling with make -C src cluster.o REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors for malloc/free declared in src/server.h. Remove the unused slot_buffer, or allocate it with zmalloc and release both paths with zfree.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails, and the allocation bypasses Redis used_memory tracking.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free violates zmalloc mandate and breaks -Werror build
